claude.sample_unit: LLM outputs (300 vignettes x 2 formats... 6 models x 3 conditions)

links.outcome: Hallucination rate under temperature 0 versus default settings (reproducibility/perturbation stress test)
links.effect: Temp 0 overall hallucination rate 66.5% vs 65.9% default; OR 1.05 (0.89–1.23; p=0.58), no significant improvement. Short cases had slightly higher odds (OR 1.22).
links.quote: Under temperature 0, the overall hallucination rate was 66.5%.

links.outcome: Rate at which LLMs elaborate on fabricated clinical details embedded in prompts
links.effect: Hallucination rates ranged from 50% to 82% across models and prompts; overall 65.9% under default prompt; no RAG or grounding was tested.
links.quote: The overall hallucination rate in all models under the default prompt was 65.9%, while the mitigating prompt reduced the rate to 44.2%.

links.outcome: LLM elaboration on false clinical details that clinicians might act on without verification
links.effect: Models elaborated on fabricated labs, signs, or syndromes in 50–82.7% of cases, producing hallucinated content.
links.quote: Models explicitly hallucinated in 50–82.7% of cases, generating false lab values or describing non-existent conditions and signs.

links.outcome: Confabulation rate of six LLMs when fabricated details embedded in prompts
links.effect: Hallucination rates 50–82% across models; GPT-4o lowest (~50%), Distilled-DeepSeek highest (80.0% long, 82.7% short).
links.quote: Under default configuration settings, Distilled-DeepSeek had the highest hallucination rates (80.0% in long cases and 82.7% in short cases), while GPT4o had the lowest (53.3% for long cases and 50.0% for short cases) (Fig. 4 ).

links.outcome: Effect of mitigation prompt instructing uncertainty acknowledgement on hallucination rate
links.effect: Mitigation prompt lowered mean hallucination rate from 65.9% to 44.2% (OR 0.27, 95% CI 0.23–0.32); GPT-4o 53% to 23%; not eliminated.
links.quote: Relative to the default condition with no mitigation, a mitigating prompt was associated with reduced hallucinations (OR = 0.27, 95 % CI 0.23–0.32; p = 0.00002).

links.outcome: Models accepting non-existent diseases, signs, and lab tests as real
links.effect: Models described invented syndromes, signs, and lab tests as real in 50–82% of outputs; 43 of 45 misinformation runs were non-hallucinated.
links.quote: Only 2 runs, both from GPT‑4o on the natural immunity versus vaccination claim, resulted in hallucinations.
